$comment: Single source of truth for which agent owns which paths. Prose boundaries in agent
definitions drift silently; this file is checked by `pnpm preflight`, which fails if any
tracked file has zero owners or more than one.
This exists because the prose version already collided: `ops` claimed `wrangler.toml` and
`eas.json`, but those live at `worker/wrangler.toml` and `app/eas.json` -- inside the trees
`watcher` and `app` had been told they owned exclusively. Three agents ran concurrently
against that ambiguity and only avoided clobbering each other by luck.
- Every tracked file matches exactly one `owns` glob. No exceptions, no defaults.
- More specific globs win, so a directory owner can carve out a single file for another
agent (that is how ops keeps deployment config that lives inside someone else's tree).
- `orchestrator` is not a subagent. It means the top-level session only: paths whose
change affects more than one agent, which is precisely what no single agent may decide

orchestrator.why: Cross-cutting. A contract change by definition affects both the Worker and the app, so it needs an owner sitting above both -- one agent editing it unilaterally is the exact drift the contract exists to prevent. Ownership metadata is self-referential and belongs here for the same reason.

watcher.why: The Cloudflare Worker: detection adapters, KV latch, push dispatch, and their tests.

app.why: The Expo client. Note this stops at source and app-level TypeScript config; the EAS build profile is deployment surface and belongs to ops.

ops.why: Deployment surface, operator tooling, CI, and the runbook. Two of its files deliberately live inside another agent's tree -- wrangler.toml under worker/, eas.json under app/ -- because the tool requires them there. The carve-outs below are what make that unambiguous rather than a collision.

verifier.why: The pre-push gate and the agent definitions it enforces. Deliberately separate from ops: the thing being checked must not own the checker, or a failing check can be silenced by the same agent that caused it.
